approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a carbon within the same six-member ring. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch permitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while keeping a separate best archive. Memory records signed changes in rooted one-bond environments, keeps up to four inverse attributes from each selected transition, and vetoes a proposal when both signs match one live transition. These environments record atom properties and bond order but omit whether a bond belongs to a ring.
approach.novelty: Make inverse memory distinguish cyclic and acyclic versions of the same local environment by adding a binary ring-membership flag to every bond in its rooted motif. Ring and chain occurrences will then receive separate signed counts and restriction keys. The original motif description remains the ordering prefix, so the addition preserves priority between existing motif families. Earlier memory siblings changed sign coverage, score-based credit, count-based ranking, overlap retention or occurrence boundaries; they retained the same pooled structural descriptions. This experiment changes the topological context of the remembered attribute. It keeps the Parent's graph generation and nitrogen relocation mechanism.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes the supplied panel with macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population standard deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its radius-one star describes each root-to-neighbor bond by order alone, so cyclic and acyclic occurrences with identical atom labels contribute to the same motif count and inverse restriction. A passive reconstruction of all fifteen Parent task logs reproduces 4545 valid novel tests, 195 vetoes, 435 installations and 1711 retained attributes with zero count, selection or veto reconstruction errors. Across the normalized batch-source and tested-candidate graphs, 821 of 3119 distinct old motif types have more than one binary cycle-spoke annotation, yielding 4158 refined types. One observed degree-two oxygen star, with one methylene neighbor and one carbonyl-carbon neighbor, occurs with both bonds outside rings and with both bonds in rings. Under the exact annotated descriptor and unchanged memory rules specified below, separate tables driven by the same recorded selected transitions retain 1711 attributes, change seven installations' projected old-family selections, and veto 178 rather than 195 draws. The 17 changed raw decisions cover 15 batches in ten sessions and put 15 distinct additional task-local identities into reconstructed complete first-ten prefixes; repeated or cutoff-excluded draws are not extra members. They comprise seven ring-opening, four ring-closing, three path-addition and three atom-change draws. These are unscored conditional allocation measurements, not an alternative scored walk. Earlier siblings n-a240f72e3717 and n-7c411fdf5a88 relaxed credit or signature coverage and lost paired means 0.020273360127168 and 0.039186838732539676. Turnover credit in n-f37b5cf41e6f lost 0.002455559942229346; independent overlap retention in n-52759efc37a6 changed one scored batch and missed its target. The more recent count-boundary sibling n-ccfeef46a581 admitted eleven evaluated neighbors but lost about 0.026119 in paired mean. Those results show that fewer vetoes or more quantitative matching alone is insufficient, while leaving the observed pooling of different cycle contexts unresolved.
hypothesis: Refine each rooted radius-one motif with binary cycle membership of its root-to-neighbor bonds, so signed occurrence counts and inverse tabu restrictions distinguish cyclic from acyclic instances of an otherwise identical local environment.

finding_summary.headline: Separating ring and chain motifs changed 20 evaluated neighbors, but all three seeds lost score
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out lack of structural activation or lack of evaluated exposure as the explanation for the missing score benefit. The original labels really did pool ring and chain occurrences, and the refined labels still transferred restrictions between distinct molecules during a live memory window. That additional topological distinction alone did not improve this search. It also did more than remove vetoes: resolving opposite changes that previously canceled changed which motif families were retained in nine transitions and created one extra veto. The largely unfavorable outcomes of the newly allocated neighbors show why passive admissions cannot be treated as evidence of useful search. The full trajectories also change when a batch stops on a different draw, so the large final losses do not identify the causal score contribution of any single annotation or unscored alternative. The supplied molecular assessment still finds aromatic and carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry. Binary cycle membership does not describe ring size, geometry, strain or chemical stability; those limitations remain open after this experiment.
finding_summary.results: The observed graphs contained 834 old motif families with multiple cycle contexts, and those distinctions reached live restrictions and scored proposals. A separate unannotated memory replay on the same sources and accepted history shows that 19 evaluated molecules were newly admitted and one evaluated molecule replaced a newly vetoed ring opening, changing 20 of 435 actual batches. Only one of these 20 molecules improved its source, by 0.001295; 19 worsened it and none tied. None immediately improved the best archive. One worsening ring closure became the next walk state, but its 20 later evaluated descendants added no archive gain. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.476854, a paired loss of 0.044906 instead of the required gain of 0.002. All three seeds declined. DRD2 and sitagliptin accounted for the largest task losses; zaleplon improved slightly on average.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl scaffolds persist, but high scores also accompany reactive decorations, sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-9dc03aaf234b produces medium-sized to large, heavily branched ring systems: recognizable indole/benzofuran/benzothiophene carbonyl compounds, decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked cyclic amines, bridged amides and sulfur-dense cages. All five tasks are covered. Each digest contains 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals, across seeds 0, 1 and 2. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9057, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7264 in the supplied task order; these are fractions of strings containing aromatic tokens, not aromatic-atom fractions or evidence that every leading molecule is aromatic. Every set has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral SMILES can contain basic amines, and these records do not reveal protonation or stereochemical processing inside an evaluator. There is meaningful variation between seeds and tasks, but high-scoring excerpts commonly comprise close relatives of a few frameworks. An ordinary indole carboxamide is reasonably recognizable synthetic chemistry; many other leaders combine unusual sulfur coordination, heteroatom-halogen bonds or tightly connected bridges whose makeability is questionable. These coexist with useful-looking aromatic and carbonyl arrangements. The chemistry remains broadly similar to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc even where particular structures and recorded scores differ. All supplied child and parent trajectories were read passively. Structural sizes below are atom counts derived from their saved SMILES; scores are copied from those trajectories or the digest. The audit at .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-04-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json records input hashes, graph readings and exact digest-to-trajectory matches. The digest final_molecules entries are the last evaluated neighbors of seed 2, not the best archive or all seeds combined. Missing features below distinguish absent chemical quality from demonstrated score requirements: these data cannot identify an unseen target pharmacophore, prove synthesis or establish biological activity.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms. Compact fused aromatic heterocycles linked through an amide or ketone to a phenyl ring are prominent: the 0.39905049777278273 indole carboxamide has ethoxy, methyl and thiol substituents, while the 0.41003927643747895 benzofuran relative carries an anilide, an aminochloromethyl group, an aniline nitrogen and an N-chloro amide. Other strong examples replace the heteroaromatic core with bridged unsaturated O/N/S rings. The 0.3984261621341843 ketone is a considerably more entangled sulfur-containing polycycle. Ordinary aryl amides are plausible starting chemistry; the chlorinated nitrogen and unusual bridged sulfur products are much less convincing synthetic endpoints. Ring-token presence is universal and aromatic-token presence is 0.9057; this is not a ring-poor search.
liabilities: The highest displayed benzofuran compound includes an N-chloro amide and an aminochloromethyl substituent; these are chemical reactivity concerns distinct from ordinary carbon-bound aryl chlorine.
Thiols, unusual multiply bonded sulfur, highly bridged unsaturated frameworks and the cyclic alkyne-containing low example raise stability or geometric concerns.
Potential configurations in the aminochloromethyl and bridged products are unspecified; the proposal stereocentre-token rate is 0.0.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the useful aromatic-carbonyl connection through late structural changes; some low neighbors lose it while retaining many rings and heteroatoms.

A wider set of stable matched versions of the compact heteroaromatic carbonyl framework without N-halogen substitution or unusual sulfur bridges. Conventional indole amides already occur, so the missing capability is sustained chemically coherent variation, not access to aromatic rings or amides.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. Its higher-scoring relatives retain a relatively compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. Low examples with a tetrahedral aminoalkyl linkage instead of the intact amide carbonyl score 0.03343008011310944 and 0.04832573556546499. The 0.0083275363022723 low example combines disrupted fused-ring chemistry, a small nitrogen ring and a cyclic alkyne-containing sulfur appendage. These comparisons support preservation of carbonyl connectivity and a coherent aromatic framework, although several substitutions change together. They do not establish that N-chlorination, a thiol or a sulfur bridge is required. Parent and child share the displayed 0.39905049777278273 and 0.41003927643747895 leaders. In seed 0 the recorded peak changes from the 0.393567030299894 benzothiophene ketone to the 0.3984261621341843 bridged ketone; that structural change does not itself demonstrate better makeability. The displayed final sulfur-cage neighbors still include a low 0.11267802872031613 example.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest proposal families, with 30-47 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length 70.4 and maximum length 92. Every proposed string contains rings and aromatic atoms. Nitrogen-rich fused aromatic carbonyl/thione cores carry substituted azaaryl groups through amine-containing linkers, together with long branched ether, ester or sulfur-containing tails. The displayed seed-0 leaders combine a chlorinated azaaryl group, a methylidene imine, a fused carbonyl/thione system, N-bromination and a fluoromethyl substituent. Seed-2 leaders use a different azaaryl/dicarbonyl arrangement and cyclic O-S-O connectivity. Ordinary heteroaromatic and carbonyl fragments are present, but their heavily decorated combinations, reactive terminal groups and unspecified side-chain configurations make the complete molecules questionable synthetic targets.
liabilities: N-bromo and N-chloro heterocycles, terminal S-Cl bonds and an O-Cl terminus occur in displayed strong molecules. Their presence must not be conflated with ordinary aryl halogenation.
Unprotected imines, unusual sulfur-carbon double-bond substitution and long multiply substituted tails introduce stability and synthesis concerns.
The decorated tails contain potential stereogenic sites but all proposal strings have stereocentre-token rate 0.0.
missing_features: A simpler, stable realization of the favorable azaaryl/amine/carbonyl arrangement across the displayed leaders; the score plateau leaves substantial decoration chemically unmotivated.

Systematic variation of ordinary linker and side-chain chemistry that preserves the conjugated core without simultaneously introducing reactive terminal bonds. The trajectories do not identify a unique unseen scaffold required by this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. Lower optimizer examples at 0.526081691583997, 0.5286081645773063 and 0.5300762397705813 alter its fused-ring connectivity, carbonyl/imine pattern or conjugation. Higher molecules retain substantial nitrogen-containing aromatic and carbonyl/thione organization while adding different azaaryl decoration. The displayed leaders at evaluations 257, 269, 278, 279, 288, 294, 295 and 299 of seed 0 all score 0.6091282178833478 despite changes to sulfur substitution, branching, bromination or terminal heteroatom-halogen groups. This plateau gives no evidence that those extra decorations are individually needed. The final seed-2 example with disrupted azaaryl aromaticity scores 0.541787206685953, whereas the displayed nitrogen-linked aromatic relative reaches 0.6084360836298065; connectivity also differs, so aromaticity alone is not isolated. Relative to the parent, seed-0 peak structures remain decorated azaaryl fused heterocycles, but the recorded peak is 0.6091282178833478 versus 0.6161710037174721. The child has a smaller maximum proposal size than the parent, while still retaining reactive decorations; size reduction alone has not produced an ordinary medicinal series.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 32-43 heavy atoms; all contain aromatic tokens, rings and halogens. Early molecules are biaryl carboxylic acid/amides with a sulfonylated pyrrolidine. Strong later molecules have substantially different nitrogen and sulfur connections: a 0.8500094650652374 family places an ordinary tertiary azetidine nitrogen between a substituted aryl-containing chain and a small sulfur/nitrogen ring bearing an aryl thioamide. A separate 0.868020189804352 family is a dense bridged aryl/N/S structure with brominated phenyl regions and a substituted sulfur ring. Basic carbon-bound amines therefore are present, although not every nitrogen is an ordinary basic amine. The aromatic portions are familiar, but strained small rings, unusual sulfur valence and the overall bridged architectures make many complete products difficult to regard as plausible medicinal compounds.
liabilities: Small saturated N/S rings, multiply connected bridges and sulfur centers with unusual multiple bonding raise geometric and stability concerns.

Displayed strong molecules combine thiols, thioamides and terminal sulfur-halogen bonding with highly halogenated aromatic regions; a high recorded score does not establish acceptable reactivity or solubility.
The displayed leaders contain potential stereogenic relationships but no proposal includes a stereocentre token. Their actual three-dimensional configurations are unresolved.
missing_features: Convincing stable whole-molecule versions of the observed aryl/cyclic-amine arrangements, retaining their useful spacing while replacing strained or unusual sulfur connections. Some ordinary carbon replacements are already score-tolerated locally.

Defined stereochemical identities for constrained products. Emitted strings also show no charged forms, but these records cannot establish whether the evaluator considered protonation or whether an explicitly charged proposal would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low displayed acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives score 0.007468397818197266 to 0.011875520467584314, far below the nitrogen-containing sulfur-rich leaders. This is consistent with a different arrangement of hydrophobic rings and nitrogen centers, together with loss or transformation of acidic/carbonyl functionality; it is not proof of a specific binding interaction. A basic center by itself is insufficient: the initial N-methylpiperidine/hydroxamate compound scores 0.0003786988088202195. The two displayed 0.8500094650652374 molecules replace an aryl-linked substituted sulfur center with the corresponding carbon center while preserving that recorded score. Several neighboring sulfur/carbon variants also share 0.8302140284961123. Thus the observed score does not require every unusual sulfur linkage. The 0.868020189804352 bridged leader is identical to the parent seed-1 leader. Seed 2 has a recorded peak of 0.47197342727666497 versus the parent 0.9148143511682032, yet its final molecules remain complex amine-bearing sulfur cages; the changed score accompanies a different arrangement within the same broad problematic chemistry, not loss of all rings or nitrogen.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals range from 27 to 45 heavy atoms, with mean SMILES length 61.4. All contain rings and aromatic atoms. The highest displayed family combines an alkyl-substituted azaaryl ring and an aryl group with bridged unsaturated amide/urea-containing rings. The 0.20981104279018886 leader has an N-methyl carbonyl-containing ring and an N-N-O bridge; related entries vary a bridge methylene, alkyl branches or the N/O sequence. Other seeds retain aryl carbonyl families but add sulfur-containing bridges, hydrazine-like connections, alcohol/ether substituents and halogenation. These molecules have recognizable constituent fragments, yet the medium and larger bridged loops and unusual heteroatom junctions make complete synthesis and geometry questionable.
liabilities: The leading series closes several interdependent medium or larger loops between an azaaryl region and an amide-containing ring; graph connectivity alone does not establish feasible geometry.
N-N-O bridges and a displayed O-O linkage introduce potential chemical lability; lower examples also contain O-Br and unusual sulfur junctions.
The final sulfur-rich bridged products and the highest N/O-bridged family have no specified stereochemistry.
missing_features: Stable bridge and linker alternatives that retain the observed aryl/azaaryl/carbonyl arrangement without requiring contiguous N-N-O or peroxide-containing connections.
Geometrically credible constrained analogues with specified configurations. More rings or more aromatic atoms alone is not the supported missing feature.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl compound scores 0.1678386594791329. Ring-opened aromatic compounds with exposed carbonyl/urea chains score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515. The higher bridged azaaryl/aryl examples therefore suggest that the relative arrangement and constraint of aromatic and carbonyl groups matters more than simply adding aromatic atoms. Within that family, the methylene-containing leader scores 0.20981104279018886, the closely related urea/N-N-O bridge 0.20775769309691736, the shorter N-O bridge 0.2056349053193895 and the peroxide-containing bridge 0.20647766243219587. The proximity of those scores does not establish that extra N-N or O-O bonding is necessary. Child and parent share the displayed 0.20775769309691736 and 0.2056349053193895 molecules. Their seed-0 peak values are 0.20981104279018886 and 0.21196904390980506, respectively, within related bridged aromatic/carbonyl chemistry. The final seed-2 sulfur-containing examples remain lower than the displayed leaders, including 0.18814867381840605; the final list is not an archive.

per_task.generated_character: These proposals are relatively compact in atom count, with 25-33 heavy atoms, but often extremely dense topologically. Aromatic-token presence is 0.7264 across all proposals; the leading 0.48118636011729826 molecule itself has no aromatic atoms on parsing. It is an unsaturated sulfur-rich cage with carbonyl groups, a fluoromethyl substituent, an acyl fluoride and a sulfinamide-type substituent. Other strong examples contain N-F bonds, imino nitrogen, sulfur-carbon multiple bonds and overlapping small heterocycles. The highest product has formula C14H15F2N3O3S8, illustrating that compactness here does not mean ordinary carbon-based drug chemistry. Its unusual sulfur coordination, interlocked rings and unspecified configurations make synthesis and physical realizability especially questionable.
liabilities: Numerous unusual sulfur-carbon multiple bonds and sulfur-containing bridges are concentrated into small overlapping rings; successful parsing is not evidence of a stable isolable cage.
Displayed leaders include reactive acyl fluoride, sulfinyl fluoride, N-F and N-S connections in complicated combinations.
Potential stereochemical relationships at saturated carbon and unusual sulfur centers are unassigned, despite the strong geometric constraints.
missing_features: Stable, geometrically credible realizations of the compact carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement seen in stronger products. The displayed high scores are carried largely by sulfur cages, not a demonstrated series of ordinary saturated heterocycles.

Chemically controlled alternatives to reactive acyl-fluoride, sulfinyl-fluoride and N-fluoro substitutions while preserving polar-group placement. Their benefit remains to be tested; the records do not support prescribing an unseen target-specific amine or aromatic fragment.

Specified feasible configurations for the highly constrained products. The present score gradient cannot establish a preferred stereoisomer because the emitted examples leave those identities undefined.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic dicarbonyl compound scores 0.0020944534688323298, and a larger aromatic ring-expanded carbonyl relative scores 7.590554525032884e-10. Higher structures are generally more compact heteroatom-rich cages with altered saturation, nitrogen/carbonyl connectivity and fluorine placement. However, sulfur-rich cages also occur among extremely low examples, including 3.046653569109811e-09, so neither sulfur loading nor ring density is sufficient. A particularly direct displayed comparison changes the acyl-fluoride carbonyl carbon of the 0.48118636011729826 leader to sulfur, giving the sulfinyl-fluoride relative at 0.43569274814003056. The observed score favors that carbonyl version over further sulfur substitution, without establishing that either reactive fluoride group is desirable medicinal chemistry. The parent contains the same 0.48118636011729826 leader and the 0.4413006791220245 seed-2 heterocycle. Its seed-1 peak is 0.5903526424693334 versus the child 0.4075035943835411, with dense sulfur ring chemistry persisting in both. Final seed-2 proposals still include scores 0.013831016286412501 and 0.008325219488378631, showing that superficially similar sulfur-rich connectivity can be poorly rewarded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Displayed strong products retain N-halogen, O-halogen or S-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur multiple bonding and densely connected heteroatom junctions. Yet a carbon-linked and a sulfur-linked aryl/cyclic-amine pair both score 0.8500094650652374, and replacing an acyl carbonyl carbon with sulfur changes 0.48118636011729826 to 0.43569274814003056. Thus unusual sulfur is not uniformly required by the observed feedback. Ordinary amides and carbon-bound amines are already accessible; their coherent combination with stable surrounding chemistry remains incomplete.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently turn favorable aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements into complete molecules with conventional bond chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand matched ordinary carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and conventional sulfur alternatives while preserving the useful attachment pattern. Distinguish heteroatom-halogen bonds and unusual sulfur coordination from ordinary aryl halides, sulfides, sulfoxides and sulfones. Assess the resulting complete structures through the same observed feedback; local element substitution alone does not establish chemical quality.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All proposal sets have ring_closure_rate 1.0. The output includes bridged N/O amides, small N/S rings, cyclic alkyne-containing appendages and sulfur cages. Carbonyl-disrupted aromatic relatives score 0.03343008011310944 and 0.04832573556546499, while ring-opened carbonyl-chain examples score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515 below related constrained aromatic/carbonyl families. Dense ring content is therefore neither the missing resource nor sufficient evidence of a useful arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator supplies abundant cycles but does not consistently preserve useful functional-group geometry in plausible ring and linker arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent variations in ring size, fusion, bridge connectivity and linker length that preserve promising carbonyl and heteroatom attachment relationships. Include ordinary less strained ring alternatives alongside constrained ones. Treat geometric feasibility and functional-group integrity as molecular properties to investigate, rather than equating any cycle with a satisfactory ring system.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Decorated nitrogen-heterocycle relatives share 0.6091282178833478 across changes to branching, sulfur centers and reactive terminal groups. A separate carbon/sulfur linker pair shares 0.8500094650652374. Bridged N/O carbonyl compounds remain close at 0.20775769309691736, 0.2056349053193895 and 0.20647766243219587 even when the bridge includes an extra nitrogen or peroxide linkage. These observations do not show that every appendage or labile bond contributes useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Score-tolerated local simplifications are not consistently combined into simpler, chemically coherent whole molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched simplifications that remove unnecessary branches and replace labile connections while holding the principal scaffold and polar-group positions fixed. Include complete combinations of locally tolerated ordinary replacements, using actual feedback to learn whether their combined simplification remains useful. Do not assume that a tie for one local change proves a benefit for an untested whole molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Displayed examples include an aminochloromethyl substituent, substituted saturated amine rings, N/O bridges and interlocked sulfur cages. These graphs contain potential stereochemical relationships, but the saved identities specify no configurations. The same problem occurs in several structures shared with the parent; a changed graph or score has not resolved it.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted identities leave stereochemical and geometric relationships undefined in many constrained products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make feasible stereochemical identities accessible and preserve their definitions through structural edits, using only the candidate molecular graph and ordinary feedback. Pair configuration handling with alternatives whose bridge and ring geometry is credible; assigning tags to an implausible cage would not repair its chemistry. Any score sensitivity to configuration must be established empirically.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
